quest.title: "Savior"
quest.description: Facing the Abyss Order's assault on Natlan, you decide to return to the cave where the key was lost, seeking a chance to end the conflict...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1125, Mora x49200, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x9

chapter.title: A Space and Time for You

talks.objective: Return to the area near the cave to investigate

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And we're back where we started. That hilichurl probably found the key nearby, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's look around for clues. There's no time to waste — Iansan and Citlali are waiting for us!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... We've scoured the entire area, but still nothing. How the heck did the key end up in that hilichurl's hands?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Are we supposed to believe that it just fell out of your {M#sister}{F#brother}'s pocket as {M#she}{F#he} passed by?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hah. Seems kinda ludicrous to lose something so important in such a dumb way... But then again, who knows? Sometimes in life, things just go missing and that's that.
Ah! Thank goodness, someone's here... Please, help me!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Who are you? What happened?
Uh...
Ah, ugh, no, now isn't the time...
Please, you gotta help me... I'm being chased by monsters, and I can't keep running. Can you do something?

choices.text: You've come to the right person.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, where are they? Paimon doesn't see any monsters behind you...
Huh...? I'm sorry, I don't quite understand...
They're almost here... This really isn't the time to be joking around...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... We're not... We're completely serious. We don't see any monsters.
But how... Ugh, there's no time! They're coming. We gotta run!

choices.text: But I really don't see anything...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's wrong with that girl? She must be seeing things...
ARGH!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh no! It looks like something really hit her... maybe she was right!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Quick, let's see if she's okay!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's wrong? Are you hurt? What was that?
The monsters... They're right there. You need to get out of here, it's too dangerous!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let me help you up first...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Huh!?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Suddenly... I can see them...)
Huh? Oh, now you finally see them? Well, it's about time... I nearly kicked the bucket just now...

choices.text: I'm sorry...

response.text: Great! Thank you, Savior!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ..."Savior"?

choices.text: I'll take care of them now.
Where do you intend to run to?
But... where are these monsters you speak of?

dialogues.speaker: Sutura
dialogues.text: Wow! "Tuma{RUBY#[S]Hope}ini," our hero! We've actually fought together before. You probably don't remember it though, hahaha...

choices.text: Of course I do.

response.speaker: Sutura
response.text: You do? Then it's truly an honor to serve alongside you once more.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thank you for standing guard this whole time.

response.speaker: Sutura
response.text: It's all good! Honestly, it's not been that much work. Haven't heard a peep from the enemy.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Have you seen anything out of the ordinary?

response.speaker: Sutura
response.text: Nothing that would indicate an impending attack. I've spotted a bunch of Abyss Order operatives, but they weren't acting hostile, just hanging around.

response.speaker: Sutura
response.text: There were even moments when they seemed to be meditating. At least, that's what it looked like to me. Maybe it's part of their religion, or something.

response.speaker: Sutura
response.text: Out of an abundance of caution, I asked some shamans from the tribe to take a look, and see if there was anything nefarious at work...

response.speaker: Sutura
response.text: But, they didn't sense anything untoward. So we just put it down to religious ceremony and left them to it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Interesting... Well, the more time they spend meditating, the less time they spend trying to beat us to a pulp.

choices.text: It seems suspicious, though...

response.speaker: Sutura
response.text: Heh, well, the shamans didn't raise any concerns, so how bad could it be? Far as I'm concerned, so long as they don't pose an active threat, they can do all the cult-worship activities they want.

response.speaker: Sutura
response.text: Besides, as soon as everything's in place and we're ready for an all-out offensive, they'll be no match for us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Sounds like morale is pretty high. Guess there's strength and confidence in numbers. Let's keep going, {NICKNAME}.

choices.text: Could this be related to their true objective?
Yeah, sorry. I don't recall.

response.speaker: Sutura
response.text: Haha, that's to be expected! You took point, and I was much further back in the ranks. I saw you, though... You were a great inspiration to us all.

talks.objective: Talk to the girl attacked by the monster

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Umm? You done? Paimon still can't see anything, so she can't tell.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It just looked like you were slicing at thin air. Kinda funny, actually...

choices.text: I don't know what's going on, either...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, really?

choices.text: Let's try it one more time.

response.text: Sure.
Ah...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What's wrong?
I—It's nothing! It's okay, I can see they're all gone now. No need for you to check.
I didn't think much of it when the monsters were breathing down our necks, but now that I've calmed down... holding hands with you like this... I'm just a little shy, that's all.

choices.text: Oh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Have you never shaken hands with someone before? You sure get flustered easily...

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Well, I... Anyway. I haven't had the chance to introduce myself yet. I'm Direidyth. Thanks for saving me just now. I'm really grateful for your help.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #No worries! Paimon's Paimon, and this is {NICKNAME}. With {M#him}{F#her} around, you'll be safe from any monsters — as long as they're visible!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... What was the deal with those monsters just now, anyway?

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Your guess is as good as mine... I could see them the whole time, so when you said you couldn't, I thought you were making fun of me...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, that must have been scary... The idea that we'd stand by and laugh while some poor girl was being hunted down by monsters...

choices.text: That would've made us more monstrous than the monsters.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mm-hmm!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, we aren't like that. When we say we can't see something, it's because we really can't see it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But more importantly, did the monsters hurt you? How bad is it?

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: It's nothing serious, hehe... but I did sprain my ankle back there. I won't be doing any more running for a while...

choices.text: There's a cave nearby.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good idea! We'll take you.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Phew... Thank you so much. Despite getting injured, I still feel much safer with you around.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: I'm gonna stay here until I heal up. Don't wanna risk running into any more monsters...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, you already took a big enough risk coming out here all on your own! Where are you from, Direidyth?

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: A small village... far away from here. I walked for what seemed like forever, and lost my way, so... yeah, I have no idea where I am anymore.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Maybe all these trials and tribulations are part of the journey... no one said finding the Savior is gonna be easy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #...That's the second time you've called {NICKNAME} a "Savior." What's all that about?

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Oh, sorry, it just slipped out — I was caught off guard. The resemblance is so uncanny...

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Um, anyway... Let me start from the beginning.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: There was once a sage who passed through my village. People got the sense that she was truly omniscient.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: The sage said that... doomsday was coming, but as that day approached, a Savior would reveal themselves to us.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: The day of disaster is almost upon us. So my grandmother begged me to leave the village and find the Savior before it's too late.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Doomsday...?

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: I've heard people talk about the Savior since I was a kid. Growing up, it really made an impression on me. The description is practically etched into my mind...

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: So, when I saw your golden hair for the first time... It was like this image that's existed in my mind's eye all these years suddenly came to life. Everything matched...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Ohh... So that's why you were lost for words when you first saw {M#him}{F#her}.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well, {NICKNAME}'s definitely got what it takes to be a "Savior." And {M#he}{F#she}'s already got a ton of titles, so {M#he}{F#she} won't mind one extra.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: #Um, actually I don't think it's {M#him}{F#her}.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? But didn't you say that everything matched?

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: #Everything, except the gender. The Savior was described as a {M#young woman}{F#young man}.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, for goodness' sake... There are gender requirements to be a Savior? Really?

choices.text: I think I know who it is.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Oh, of course! If it's not you, then it's gotta be {M#her}{F#him}!

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Who? Who is it?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #My {M#sister}{F#brother}.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: #You have a {M#sister}{F#brother}!? Well then, that's it! It's {M#her}{F#him}, it has to be! Oh, thank goodness!

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: #Please, can you take me to see {M#her}{F#him}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Heh... Maybe, if you're lucky. It just depends if we can find {M#her}{F#him}.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: #Huh? But isn't {M#she}{F#he} your {M#sister}{F#brother}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Sorry, looks like Paimon's steered this conversation back to the fallout between you two... It wasn't on purpose, but that's the reality... so it's hard to avoid...

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: #Okay, fair enough... But since you're looking for {M#her}{F#him} anyway, why don't we team up? We might stand a better chance if we work together.

choices.text: Have you always believed that doomsday will come?

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Yes. Everyone says that the disaster is inevitable.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: But the Savior will rescue us all from our pain and suffering... I've always dreamed of meeting the Savior.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do you really buy this whole doomsday thing? Seems kinda far-fetched...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (She spoke with conviction... I don't think she's lying.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Maybe it's another lie spread by the Abyss Order?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (See? She broke eye contact. Sure sign of a guilty conscience! Time to press her for answers.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's wrong, Direidyth? Something's clearly bothering you. You wanna tell us what's going through your mind?

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Oh... I just...

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: How should I put it...?

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Hmm...

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: #{NICKNAME} looks just like the Savior of my dreams...

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: And it's not every day that the Savior of your dreams swoops in and saves the day in your moment of crisis.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: So, I... I'm just a little overwhelmed, that's all. Three seconds of unbroken eye contact is the limit. I don't think my mind and body can handle any more than that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What do you mean, "limit"? What happens after three seconds?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (How am I supposed to respond to that...)

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: ...I'm sorry, please forget that I said anything. Let's just... leave it there for now.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Like I said, I'm going to hide here until I feel well enough to move again.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: If you manage to find the Savior in the meantime, please, PLEASE come and let me know! Thank you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you sure you'll be okay here on your own? Do you have enough to eat?

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: I... I'll be fine! I might not be much of a fighter, but I know how to stay hidden. And if I get hungry... I'm sure I'll find something around here, don't worry about that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright then... Well, take care. Being on your own isn't easy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What a mysterious girl... We should definitely keep an eye on her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #But hey, at least she seems to like you. And it sounds like she's gonna help look for your {M#sister}{F#brother} once she's healed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, this is probably all the progress we're gonna make for now. Let's head back to the Masters of the Night-Wind and see if they need our help.

choices.text: Have you always believed that the Savior will come?
There's someone out there who matches all the requirements.
Why don't we rest there for now?
I'd never do something so horrendous.
Didn't mean to make you uncomfortable.
I want to check that I got all the monsters.
But I could see them once I held her hand.

talks.objective: Go to the Masters of the Night-Wind

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Oh, you're back! How did it go? Find anything?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nothing substantial, unfortunately. But we had the weirdest experience...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: So, I take it that the war's still on?

choices.text: No progress yet, I'm afraid.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: That's okay — I just wasn't sure, because things seemed to be at a standstill while you were gone.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: The Abyss Order hasn't attacked us, and since we don't know what they're planning, we haven't made a move either.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: In a word, it's a stalemate. The guards have been keeping watch around the clock, but for everyone else, you wouldn't even know we're at war.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... Really makes you wonder what the Abyss Order's thinking.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: #I was wondering, {NICKNAME}... If you have the time, could you go and pay a visit to the guards?

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: They've been working a pretty demanding schedule. I was gonna go see them myself, but I'm sure they'd appreciate a visit from the greatest hero of our time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw, but you're a great hero too, Iansan!

choices.text: Well, since you asked...

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Great. Thanks, you two.

choices.text: This is technically my sibling's fault, so...
Yes, unfortunately.

dialogues.speaker: Kantalo
dialogues.text: Huh? ...Is... Is that "Tum{RUBY#[S]Hope}aini"? What brings you here? Is this, like, uh... a meet-and-greet?

dialogues.speaker: Kantalo
dialogues.text: Um... Hahaha... I, uh... I wasn't... Ahh, I'm so nervous...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hey, come on. You'd march to war without so much as blinking. What's so scary about a chat with {NICKNAME}, hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Kantalo
dialogues.text: It's not the same thing at all! There are plenty of chances to go to war... but a one-on-one chat with our great hero? That could be a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity!

dialogues.speaker: Kantalo
dialogues.text: How can I not be nervous? What if I say something wrong? Or... Or if my posture's bad, or if I accidentally make a weird expression with my face? One bad impression can stick for life!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No one's here to judge you on your posture or your facial expressions! Relax!

dialogues.speaker: Kantalo
dialogues.text: *sigh* Alright, then...

dialogues.speaker: Kantalo
dialogues.text: Um... I'm sorry, great hero, but I have a small favor to ask...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let Paimon guess, an autograph, right? That's easy...

dialogues.speaker: Kantalo
dialogues.text: ...May I challenge you to a fight?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!? How can you be so... audacious and so sheepish at the same time? Hmm, Paimon's starting to think your nervousness is all just an act!

dialogues.speaker: Kantalo
dialogues.text: No no no, of course not... I just figured that if I don't ask now, I'll regret it for the rest of my life...

dialogues.speaker: Kantalo
dialogues.text: But I am still on patrol, so please, Great Paimon, if you wouldn't mind taking over for me for just a few minutes...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Again with the sheepish audacity! Just pick one or the other, will you!

choices.text: I think it's a fair request.

response.speaker: Kantalo
response.text: Woohoooooo! Haha!

response.speaker: Kantalo
response.text: Obviously, I never expected to win, but until now, I didn't appreciate just how great the gulf was between us...

response.speaker: Kantalo
response.text: Hahaha, I'll be bragging about the day I got to spar with "Tum{RUBY#[S]Hope}aini" for the rest of my life. Today's really my lucky day!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon can't keep up with you. Your tone has changed all over again now you've had a spar with {NICKNAME}... What gives?

response.speaker: Kantalo
response.text: Mm, well, some people connect through conversation, but we warriors bond by sparring. And now that I've had a bout with the hero, we're no longer strangers. Nothing to be nervous about anymore!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay... Well, each to their own, but Paimon's still gonna stick to conversation.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Have you noticed anything out of the ordinary?

response.speaker: Kantalo
response.text: Not at all. We haven't spotted any new enemy movements.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: As Paimon expected... Nothing here, either. Let's do another lap and get back to Iansan.

choices.text: What are you waiting for? Bring it on.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: You're back. So, did the guards find anything?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nothing much, no. Someone mentioned that the Abyss Order has been doing some kind of meditation or prayer, but apparently it seemed harmless.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon wants to lodge a complaint about one of the guards, though. His name's Kantalo...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Hmm?

choices.text: Ignore Paimon.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, you're back already? Ah, and no one thought to wake me up, huh!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In fairness, you look pretty hungover. Can't imagine anyone wanting to wake you up in that state...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I'll have you know I'm perfectly sober when I'm hungover! Uh... Okay, I'll admit that sounds strange at face value, but regardless...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: What I meant to say is — I heard something about the Abyss Order engaging in meditation?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that's right! Does that mean anything to you, Citlali?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I sensed something strange in my dream. It was vague, but... It seemed as if some "noise" had found its way into Natlan's Ley Lines...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What does that mean?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hard to say... I don't think it had any tangible effect on the Night Kingdom or on our Ley Lines, but still...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: It's like... a signal that exists on a different dimension of reality. It might not interfere with ours, or pose any detectable risk, but I just get the sense that something strange is going on.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So even someone as familiar with the Ley Lines as you can't tell what's going on...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No wonder the shamans that Sutura called to the front lines couldn't sense anything.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Iansan, I think we should go talk to the Chiefs. There's no point dragging this out. We need to take the initiative and drive the Abyss Order out of Natlan for good.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: If that's the counsel of Granny Itztli, I'm sure the Chiefs will agree. But it will still take us some time to gather the required force.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: In war, adequate planning and preparation is the key to victory.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Sure, but the finer details aren't my concern. Anyway, I'll leave you to it. Just remember to come find me when you're ready to talk to the Chiefs.

choices.text: Actually, since you're here, Citlali...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Oh? Sure, what is it?

choices.text: Have you ever heard of monsters...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Huh... You mean, only select individuals can see them? Hmm, now that's a strange one. I guess they could be... manifestations of a disturbed psyche? Or... extreme negativity, embodied in physical form?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: It could also be a simple case of dead monsters whose souls got stuck here somehow. Well, I say simple — things quickly get confusing when you start looking into monster souls. For starters, trying to figure out which classification system to use is a real pain in the—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, we get it... Granny Itztli's learning and wisdom knows no bounds. But could we just get the short answer?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hey, I was just thinking out loud! You really think I was just trying to flaunt my knowledge?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: ...Anyway, the short answer is... There are many potential explanations for the kind of phenomenon you describe. That said, it's not something I've ever encountered in all my years.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, okay. Well, if Granny Itztli's never seen it, it might as well not exist, right?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hey, I'm not THAT old!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I agree, it's hard to say what it was for sure.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Care to elaborate on what happened? This all sounds rather mysterious...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell the two about what happened...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Really? You had to hold her hand to see the monsters? Sounds a little contrived...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? That's the part that bothers you?

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Maybe the point is more that it requires direct physical contact, whether that be hand-holding or otherwise.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: But that's neither here nor there... What bothers me is, it sounds like she's convinced that your sibling, the leader of the Abyss Order... is a "Savior."

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: That really makes me question whose side this girl is on... and whether what she told you about her background is actually the truth.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Sorry if that comes across as paranoid. It's just hard not to be suspicious of everything when we're in the middle of a war...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Actually, Paimon feels like you make a fair point...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Whoever this girl is, she sounds like bad news.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, well you're clearly just jumping to conclusions!

choices.text: Do you think she's a spy?

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: It's hard to know what to make of it. A young lady all by herself, lost in the middle of nowhere... sees monsters that no one else can, calls the leader of the Abyss Order her Savior...

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: At the very least, we should remain vigilant. Keep a close watch on her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds sensible. On that note, we probably shouldn't have left her by herself in that cave...

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, we still need some time to muster our forces — maybe you could check on her if you're not busy. Just be careful.

choices.text: Might as well. She seems to trust me, after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's settled, then! Let's go check on her.

choices.text: Happy to. Although, I doubt she means us any harm.
Do you think she's some kind of weapon?
That are only visible to certain people?
I might as well ask one more question.
He wasn't a problem.

talks.objective: Return to the cave to investigate

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Here we are. Direidyth will still be here, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's so quiet, though... Uh-oh, what if Iansan was right? Maybe she never intended to stay here at all...

choices.text: Let's stay quiet...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}! Watch out!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Shoot, maybe Direidyth really is a—)

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Hey-yah!

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Ah... sorry, sorry! I didn't know it was you! I heard a noise, and I thought it was the monsters coming to get me...

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Did I hurt you? I'm so sorry, I... I wasn't thinking straight...

choices.text: If I'd thought it would hurt, I would have tried to dodge...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whew... That was scary. Paimon thought we'd walked into a trap...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe we shouldn't have sneaked in without announcing it. Then you would've known we weren't monsters.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: To be honest, I've been really on edge since you left. I just have this constant feeling that any second, the monsters are gonna come back and get me...

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: And it's not like I can run from them...

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: There's also no way to cook here. It's good you got back when you did. Another... hour and a half, and you probably would've found me starved to death.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #That's weirdly precise... Though, it does explain why your attack on {NICKNAME} was so weak.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, but if you really thought you were gonna starve or get killed by monsters, why'd you promise that you'd be okay here on your own?

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: I... Uhh... I just didn't want to lose face in front of my hero...

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: You already saved my life once. That's more than enough. I just... don't wanna come across as a constant burden.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh*... For someone on the brink of starvation, you're pretty preoccupied with your image. What's the real reason?

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: What...? Th—That is the real reason... I'm kinda baring my soul here, y'know...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Could she really just be an injured civilian?)

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Anyway... So, um... Could you make me some food now...?

choices.text: You are unbelievable...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's getting hungry now too... Go on then, you can join us for dinner.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Whew... I am so full. Thanks for saving me, again... Starvation feels like a distant memory now.

choices.text: No trouble at all...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Heh, you can really pack it away, Direidyth! Guess that explains how you had the energy to make it this far.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Oh...

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: (I tried so hard to hold back, but it looks like I still came across like a total glutton...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon didn't even realize how late it is! Hey, the night sky here is really pretty.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Yeah... And it's all thanks to you both that I'm able to relax and enjoy it.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: I was cooped up in that cave the whole time you were gone. Now I'm finally out, the air seems fresher, and the stars more beautiful than ever before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... You weren't in there THAT long...

choices.text: But she thought she was gonna starve to death...

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: When I was young, I used to lie on the roof of my house, gazing up at the stars...

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: And often, my mind would drift to this question... "Is this starry sky actually real?"

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Wait... Why would she think that? Does she know about the false sky?)

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: But my grandma would tell me, the answer to that question doesn't really matter.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: "Think of all the people in our village who spend their entire lives here," she'd say. To them, that little village is their whole world.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: And so, if it's our destiny to live beneath this sky all our lives, then whatever may or may not lie beyond — this is our world, and that sky is real to us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Paimon kinda gets you... but also not really...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Is it kind of like... how journeying with {NICKNAME} is everything to Paimon right now?

choices.text: That seems kind of right...

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: I really treasured my "world." For a really long time...

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: The village was my everything — the houses, the scenery, stories I always loved to hear about the Savior.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: But I could never bring myself to agree with grandma. Even if the village was my entire world, I still had to know what lay outside its borders!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Go you!

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Hehe, so I finally ventured out, and set off on my journey to find the Savior.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: I'm going to make my world bigger, one step at a time... And I'm not gonna stop until I've seen what's beyond the stars!

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Maybe then, I'll finally get an answer to the question I had as a child.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Beyond the stars...

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Who knows... maybe one day, I'll be sitting and chatting just like we are now, but with someone from another world.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, "one day"... Ah, if only we could tell her. But it's probably best not to open that can of worms right now.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: I need to find the Savior and protect my world. Then, I can make sure it continues to grow.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: That's the most worthwhile thing I can think of doing, so I've been giving it everything I've got!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y'know what? That's pretty cool. Paimon kinda wants to root for you now.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Ah, sorry, I got a little carried away... I always get chatty after a hearty meal. Just like my grandma, hehe...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The more we chat, the more convinced I am that she's not a bad person...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (And it doesn't sound like she's been brainwashed by the Abyss Order. Maybe we can afford to trust her?)

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Hold on... Shh! It's them! The monsters are back!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Where? Oh, still invisible, huh?

choices.text: In that case...

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: ...Can you see them now?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yeah. Stay back — I'll handle them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon still can't see anything, but please, be careful!

choices.text: Guess we gotta try that trick again.
But also not really.
The time probably passed unbearably slowly.
That's two favors you owe me now. Hope you're keeping count.
Sure. I know just the recipe. Only takes an hour and a half.
...And somehow, it still hurt less than I expected.
And move in carefully.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Wow, that was fast... Did you get all of them?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's slowly but surely getting used to the sight of you fighting thin air...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You doing alright, Direidyth?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Direidyth? Hey, it's okay, there's nothing to be scared of anymore...

dialogues.speaker: Direidyth
dialogues.text: ...Oh... I—I'm fine... I just spaced out there for a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You... spaced out? That's a pretty bold move under the circumstances...

dialogues.speaker: Direidyth
dialogues.text: #I was just, uh... The image of {NICKNAME} fighting to protect me — I was trying to commit it to memory. Seems like the least I can do.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright... Whatever floats your boat.

dialogues.speaker: Direidyth
dialogues.text: Anyway, there are no more monsters in the area, and it's getting late. Why don't you stay here tonight?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Sounds reasonable to Paimon! What do you think, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I'm personally satisfied that Direidyth isn't a threat, but... it can't hurt to monitor her for another night.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright! Direidyth, we'll be... Huh? Direidyth? Why are you going in alone?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As you stare at the Hibernation Chamber key in your hands, you start to relax and drift into a deep sleep...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Soon, a vivid dream fills your mind...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This is... the Night Kingdom?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #({M#Lumine}{F#Aether}! And... the Lord of the Night?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (My head... It hurts!)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (My headache... it's gone...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I think... I hear a voice in the darkness.)
...Doomsday... a fitting name indeed.
A blood-red sky...
Wild beasts that slaughter all in sight...
Endless pain, a terrible curse that cannot be reversed...
And... the birth of a Savior.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (That dream I just had...)

dialogues.speaker: Direidyth
dialogues.text: Ah, you're awake... I—I'm sorry, I didn't mean to, uh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Was she holding my hand?)

dialogues.speaker: Direidyth
dialogues.text: You just... looked quite distressed, like you were having a nightmare...

dialogues.speaker: Direidyth
dialogues.text: I thought if I took your hand into mine, you might find it soothing... At least, that's what my family always did when I had nightmares.

dialogues.speaker: Direidyth
dialogues.text: But it didn't seem to work on you... In fact, I think I made it even worse... I'm so sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? Is that right...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hmm... You'd better not be trying to pull a fast one on the {NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: Direidyth
dialogues.text: What!? Don't be so... I have more self-control than that!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Self-control? What does that have to do with it...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Ugh, I still can't remember anything... What did I see in my dream just now?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #(I think I saw {M#Lumine}{F#Aether} in the Night Kingdom at the very start of the dream... But I can't remember what happened next...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Never mind. If the memory is gone, I can't force myself to remember it...)

choices.text: I'm gonna go back to sleep.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... No way is Paimon getting back to sleep after this!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You go ahead, but for the rest of the night, Paimon is staying up to keep an eye on this young lady!

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Aww... Do I really seem that shady to you...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, Direidyth, this should be enough food for three days. Make sure you eat the perishable stuff first, so nothing goes to waste. ...You can tell which stuff is perishable, right?

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Yeah, I can tell from the ingredients. Thank you so much for making all this for me.

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Three days will definitely be enough time for my ankle to heal. Then, I'll continue on my journey to find the Savior.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, then we'll be off. Bye for now, Direidyth!

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: See ya... Wait, but if this is goodbye... How am I supposed to find you again?

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Oh... I mean, what if I find your sibling? How am I supposed to let you know?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, that's a good point... We share the same goal, but we're constantly on the road, so we've got no fixed address...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How about this? When the time comes, you can just write a letter to Mavuika. She'll be able to find us for sure!

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Mavuika? Who's Mavuika?

choices.text: Hold on...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's the Abyss Order! They're here!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... It doesn't look like they're marching to war. More like they're... running away?

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Where? What are you talking about?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A bunch of Abyss Order thugs... You don't see them? They're heading right this way...

choices.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: That's strange... I guess it's my turn to not be able to see the monsters.

choices.text: Hmm... I bet...

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: Ahh, you're right! I see them now... You weren't joking after all. So this is what it's like...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What a weird situation. What is making these monsters invisible? Is it Direidyth, or the monsters themselves? Or is it us?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, might as well mow these ones down. Just so they can't pose a threat to the tribes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Woohoo, all done! Their morale seemed super low... Guess they really were on the run, huh?

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: So, there's no more of them, right? I still can't wrap my mind around this... Why couldn't I see them until you took my hand?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Believe me, I'm as baffled as you are...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The plot thickens. Turns out there are also monsters which I can see, but Direidyth can't...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, any ideas on why those monsters might have been running away? Maybe something went down on the front line?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's getting a little worried about Iansan and the others... Let's head back to the Masters of the Night-Wind right away!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We gotta go! Bye for now, Direidyth!

response.speaker: Direidyth
response.text: See ya — and please, take care!

choices.text: The tried-and-tested method will allow you to see them.
Wait a second...
I think I see something over there.
We can catch up tomorrow morning.

dialogues.speaker: Direidyth
dialogues.text: Aah! ...Don't worry, I—I'm fine. I just need some time to myself...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Why holding hands? Why that, specifically? Why not... literally anything else?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: I'm not normally so suspicious of strangers, but at times like this, the safety of the tribes has to come first.
